boards.school_name: South Dakota School of Mines and Technology
boards.title: Your First Weekend at South Dakota School of Mines and Technology, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that begins on campus and moves into documented Rapid City public attractions.

cards.title: Start at the Campus Arch
cards.subtitle: Campus Quad · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: Begin with a daylight walk through the Quad and use the arch as a visual campus landmark before choosing the rest of your route.
cards.short_summary: A campus-orientation stop anchored by the Quad’s arch.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines’ institutional profile identifies the iconic arch in the Quad as an anchor of campus.
cards.access_notes: Use the university campus map to orient yourself and follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Get Oriented at Surbeck Center
cards.subtitle: Campus · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: Stop in the student center to locate dining, the bookstore, student-engagement offices, and places to sit before heading out.
cards.short_summary: The campus student-activity hub provides several practical first-weekend waypoints.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines describes Surbeck Center as the heart of student activity, with dining, a bookstore, student-engagement offices, esports, and spaces to relax.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Mines Virtual Tour & Campus Highlights
cards.access_notes: Building services and spaces may have separate availability; check campus postings when you arrive.

cards.title: Find a Study Base at Devereaux Library
cards.subtitle: Campus · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: Take a short reset in the library, then note its study spaces, makerspace, archives, and help resources for the coming week.
cards.short_summary: A useful academic-home-base stop before the weekend’s off-campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines identifies Devereaux Library as home to student study spaces, a makerspace, books, archives, and the Vanderboom Office of Student Success.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Mines Virtual Tour & Campus Highlights
cards.access_notes: Student collaboration rooms are scheduled for South Dakota Mines students; verify library hours before visiting.

cards.title: See the Current APEX Gallery Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Classroom Building 200 · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: If it is a school-year weekday, visit the gallery to see the current art-and-science exhibition; confirm the calendar before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery with changing exhibitions by artists and scientists.
cards.evidence_claim: APEX Gallery is in Classroom Building 200, is open to the public, presents art-and-science exhibitions, and lists school-year hours of Monday–Friday, 10 AM–5 PM.
cards.source_title: APEX Gallery: Art & Science Exhibitions at SD Mines
cards.access_notes: Open during the school year Monday–Friday, 10 AM–5 PM; closed in summer, on holidays, and long weekends.

cards.title: Spend a Morning with Fossils and Minerals
cards.subtitle: O’Harra Building · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: Plan this as a daytime museum visit: start with the fossil displays, then allow time for minerals, meteorites, and the Discovery Zone.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum covering regional fossils, minerals, meteorites, and hands-on exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Geology lists fossil dioramas, mineral and meteorite displays, a fluorescent mineral room, and a Discovery Zone; it lists Saturday hours in both seasonal schedules.
cards.source_title: Museum of Geology at South Dakota Mines
cards.access_notes: Listed Saturday hours are 9 AM–4:30 PM in winter and 9 AM–6 PM in summer; the museum is closed on federal holidays.

cards.title: Take a Daylight Loop on Rocker Trail
cards.subtitle: Above campus · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: Use a marked trailhead near O’Harra Stadium or Connolly Hall for a daylight walk, run, or bike ride; bring water and stay on route.
cards.short_summary: A three-mile campus-adjacent trail with marked access points and Rapid City views.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines says Rocker Trail is a three-mile walking, running, and biking loop above campus with multiple signed access points, including near O’Harra Stadium.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Mines Hosts Ribbon Cutting for New Trail Above Campus
cards.access_notes: Use marked access points in daylight and follow trail conditions and posted guidance.

cards.title: Locate the King Center
cards.subtitle: Campus · South Dakota Mines
cards.notes: Walk through the athletics and recreation hub to identify the wellness area, bouldering wall, gym, and courts for future student recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: South Dakota Mines describes King Center as its athletics hub, with a wellness center, fitness area, bouldering wall, Goodell Gym, and squash and racquetball courts.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Mines Virtual Tour & Campus Highlights
cards.access_notes: Facility and event access can vary; check current recreation or athletics information before participating.

cards.title: Climb the Hill to Dinosaur Park
cards.subtitle: Rapid City
cards.notes: Make this a daylight photo-and-view stop: follow the park paths, see the cement dinosaurs, and take in the city and Black Hills outlook.
cards.short_summary: A free hilltop park with Depression-era cement dinosaur sculptures and broad views.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City describes Dinosaur Park as a free attraction with seven cement dinosaurs on a sandstone ridge overlooking Rapid City and the Black Hills.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Free Attractions near Rapid City
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight and use established park paths around the sculptures and overlook.

cards.title: Walk the City of Presidents
cards.subtitle: Downtown Rapid City
cards.notes: Choose a few downtown corners and use the self-guided route to look closely at the life-size bronze presidential statues along the sidewalks.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-guided downtown sculpture walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City identifies the City of Presidents as a free self-guided walking tour of life-size bronze statues of past U.S. presidents along downtown streets.
cards.source_title: Top 10 Free Attractions near Rapid City
cards.access_notes: This is a self-guided outdoor walk on downtown streets and sidewalks.

cards.title: Finish with an Art Alley Walk
cards.subtitle: Between 6th and 7th Streets, Main and Saint Joseph · Downtown Rapid City
cards.notes: Walk through the public alley to view the changing murals, then leave the walls untouched unless you have obtained the required permit to add art.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown community gallery whose wall art changes regularly.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Rapid City describes Art Alley as a free, family-friendly community gallery between 6th and 7th Streets and Main and Saint Joseph Streets, with ever-changing wall art.
cards.access_notes: It is a functioning alley; stay alert for service vehicles and obtain a permit before adding artwork.
